output.summary: An aromatic, many-branched subshrub native to parts of South Africa, Zimbabwe and Mozambique, rose-scented geranium has soft, velvety, deeply cut leaves. The natural form smells minty, while cultivars may smell of rose, citrus, cinnamon, fruit, or little at all.
output.edibilityNote: The flowers and leaves are used to flavour cakes, preserves, frozen desserts, salads, sugars and teas.
